evidence.why: Wrapper sequencing and distinct PS/C invalid-axis branches.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported PS path while correcting the previously unconditional dispatch and invalid-axis description.
facts.value: Contains a non-null destination assertion, computes sinf(rad) and cosf(rad), then calls MTXRotTrig. Without DEBUG, the header maps that call to PSMTXRotTrig: it ORs the selector with 0x20, accepts X/Y/Z in either ASCII case, and leaves the destination untouched for an unsupported selector. With DEBUG, the call maps to C_MTXRotTrig, whose unsupported-axis branch invokes an assertion instead. The wrapper itself does not validate the axis before evaluating the trigonometric functions.

evidence.why: All valid branches store supplied values directly, with no normalization or consistency guard.

facts.rationale: Corrects an unconditional orthonormality claim without changing the established constructor role.
facts.value: Constructs a zero-translation 3-by-4 Cartesian-axis rotation matrix from caller-supplied sine and cosine values. For a valid axis it writes the standard X, Y or Z coefficient layout directly. The linear component is orthonormal only to the extent that the supplied values satisfy the sine/cosine unit-circle relation; the routine does not check or normalize them.

evidence.why: Computed comparison operand, ps_cmpo0/bne, reciprocal refinement, stores and return values.

facts.rationale: Preserves store-free singular failure while distinguishing the numeric branch condition from a validated mathematical-success result.
facts.value: Has no persistent state. For ordinary finite inputs, an exactly zero computed determinant takes the immediate return-zero path before any destination store; otherwise the reciprocal-refinement and output path writes all twelve elements and returns one. There is no near-singularity tolerance, finiteness test or output validation. The branch tests comparison equality, so an unordered floating-point comparison can also enter the output path if execution continues after the comparison; return one therefore indicates completion of that path, not a guarantee of a finite or numerically reliable inverse.

evidence.why: Conditional inverse-JObj and SRT product, including the Vec3 cast and persistent fighter destination.
Envelope composition and position-matrix GPU loads.

facts.rationale: Replaces the community-derived quaternion interpretation with independently read canonical call sites and preserves the supported rendering/deformation mapping.
facts.value: Supplies affine composition for fighter/model rendering and deformation. Fighter_UnkApplyTransformation_8006C0F0 conditionally builds an SRT matrix with HSD_MtxSRT and multiplies it by an inverse JObj matrix into fp->x44_mtx. The rotation argument there is passed as Vec3 despite its local Quaternion storage type, so that call is not evidence of quaternion-based SRT construction. Fighter envelope setup also concatenates joint and envelope matrices, composes the view transform, and loads the resulting position matrices for rendering.

evidence.why: Local normalization destination, unconditional calls and MWERKS-guarded matrix stores.

facts.rationale: Adds useful missing configuration and exceptional-input behavior without changing the supported axis-angle purpose.
facts.value: Computes sine/cosine and normalizes the supplied axis into a local Vec before constructing the matrix. All destination stores are inside the __MWERKS__ conditional assembly block; without that definition, the shown body performs the trigonometric and normalization calls but does not write m. It has no local null-pointer or zero-axis check and no success/failure return; degenerate-axis handling is delegated to PSVECNormalize rather than implemented here.

evidence.why: Unguarded PS reciprocal path contrasted with C assertions.

facts.rationale: Makes the PS/C validation difference explicit so the existing nonzero-quaternion description is not mistaken for runtime enforcement.
facts.value: The paired-single conversion has no null-pointer, zero-quaternion or finite-magnitude guard and returns no status. It unconditionally forms a reciprocal estimate from the squared quaternion magnitude and proceeds to matrix stores. The adjacent C_MTXQuat contains pointer and nonzero-quaternion assertions, but those checks are not present in PSMTXQuat; a nonzero, numerically usable magnitude is a precondition rather than a checked PS success condition.
